cues.say: Component 7: Sweeper and reconciliation jobs. Programs on a timer that clean up. The sweeper releases stuck things. Reconciliation compares your records with an outside source and fixes gaps. You'll bring this up during version one, when you draw the basic design.
Think of it as: Closing-time checks: count the till against the receipts. Use it for expired holds, stuck orders, and matching payments.
Here's a real scenario. 50 pizza customers reserve, then abandon the Stripe page. One paid order's webhook never arrives.
Without it: Abandoned pizzas stay reserved: lost sales.
The paid order is never cooked.
With it: Every minute, the sweeper finds expired holds.
It asks Stripe paid?; if not, the pizzas go back on sale.
Nightly: compare Stripe's payments with our orders, fix the missing one.
Why it works: Some messages always get lost. These jobs make the system end up correct anyway.
In the interview, say: Every minute, release expired holds, after asking Stripe whether they were paid.
A few related terms you may hear.
Cron: The classic name for run this on a schedule.
One runner: Only one copy runs at a time, so sweepers don't fight.
